arxiv-1405-4705.title: Central Configurations Formed By Two Twisted Regular Polygons
arxiv-1405-4705.creator: Xiang Yu and Shiqing Zhang
arxiv-1405-4705.description: A 2014 arXiv research paper by Xiang Yu and Shiqing Zhang. In this paper, we study the necessary conditions and sufficient conditions for the central configurations formed by two twisted regular polygons (one N-regular polygon and one L-regular polygon ). We wish to extend the results of the symmetrical central configurations formed by two twisted N-regular polygons, however, it will be proved that there are not more central configurations in a more general setting than the central configurations considered for some more particular situations before.

arxiv-2011-08671.title: Long-Term Pipeline Failure Prediction Using Nonparametric Survival Analysis
arxiv-2011-08671.creator: Dilusha Weeraddana(✉), Sudaraka MallawaArachchi, Tharindu Warnakula, Zhidong Li, Yang Wang
arxiv-2011-08671.description: Abstract Australian water infrastructure is more than a hundred years old, thus has begun to show its age through water main failures. Our work concerns approximately half a million pipelines across major Australian cities that deliver water to houses and businesses, serving over five million customers. Failures on these buried assets cause damage to properties and water supply disruptions.

arxiv-2102-04450.title: Noise Optimization for Artificial Neural Networks
arxiv-2102-04450.creator: Li Xiao, Zeliang Zhang, Yijie Peng
arxiv-2102-04450.description: Abstract Adding noises to artificial neural network(ANN) has been shown to be able to improve robustness in previous work. In this work, we propose a new technique to compute the pathwise stochastic gradient estimate with respect to the standard deviation of the Gaussian noise added to each neuron of the ANN.

arxiv-2307-03210.title: Sparse Graphical Linear Dynamical Systems
arxiv-2307-03210.creator: Emilie Chouzenoux emilie.chouzenoux@inria.fr, Víctor Elvira victor.elvira@ed.ac.uk
arxiv-2307-03210.description: Abstract Time-series datasets are central in numerous fields of science and engineering, such as biomedicine, Earth observation, and network analysis. Extensive research exists on state-space models (SSMs), which are powerful mathematical tools that allow for probabilistic and interpretable learning on time series.

arxiv-2309-02310.title: Quenching massive galaxies across cosmic time with the semi-analytic model Shark v2.0 2023 Quenching massive galaxies across cosmic time with the semi-analytic model Shark v2.0 – D
arxiv-2309-02310.creator: Claudia del P. Lagos, Matías Bravo, Rodrigo Tobar, Danail Obreschkow, Chris Power, Aaron S. G. Robotham, Katy L. Proctor, Samuel Hansen, Ángel Chandro-Gómez, Julian Carrivick
arxiv-2309-02310.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Claudia del P. Lagos, Matías Bravo, Rodrigo Tobar, Danail Obreschkow, Chris Power, Aaron S. G. Robotham, Katy L. Proctor, Samuel Hansen, Ángel Chandro-Gómez, Julian Carrivick. We introduce version 2.0 of the Shark semi-analytic model of galaxy formation after many improvements to the physics included.

arxiv-2402-14450.title: Bayesian games with nested information Thanks: We thank three anonymous referees for their valuable input, which helped us significantly improve the paper. We also thank Ziv Hellman, Ehud Lehrer, Dov Samet, and Omri Solan for useful discussions. Jacobovic acknowledges the support of the Israel Scien
arxiv-2402-14450.creator: Royi Jacobovic, John Yehuda Levy, Eilon Solan
arxiv-2402-14450.description: Abstract A Bayesian game is said to have nested information if the players are ordered, and each player knows the types of all players that follow her in that order. We prove that all multiplayer Bayesian games with finite actions spaces, bounded payoffs, Polish type spaces, and nested information admit a Bayesian equilibrium.

arxiv-2403-02610.title: ChatGPT4PCG 2 Competition: Prompt Engineering for Science Birds Level Generation
arxiv-2403-02610.creator: Pittawat Taveekitworachai 1 , Febri Abdullah 2 , Mury F. Dewantoro 3 , Yi Xia 4, Pratch Suntichaikul 5 , Ruck Thawonmas 6 , Julian Togelius 7 , and Jochen Renz 8
arxiv-2403-02610.description: Abstract This paper presents the second ChatGPT4PCG competition at the 2024 IEEE Conference on Games. In this edition of the competition, we follow the first edition, but make several improvements and changes. We introduce a new evaluation metric along with allowing a more flexible format for participants’ submissions and making several improvements to the evaluation pipeline.

arxiv-2405-14031.title: Energy-efficient predictive control for connected, automated driving under localization uncertainty
arxiv-2405-14031.creator: Eunhyek Joa, Eric Yongkeun Choi, Francesco Borrelli
arxiv-2405-14031.description: Abstract This paper presents a data-driven Model Predictive Control (MPC) for energy-efficient urban road driving for connected, automated vehicles. The proposed MPC aims to minimize total energy consumption by controlling the vehicle’s longitudinal motion on roads with traffic lights and front vehicles.

arxiv-2409-04962.title: A foundation model enpowered by a multi-modal prompt engine for universal seismic geobody interpretation across surveys
arxiv-2409-04962.creator: Hang Gao, Xinming Wu, Luming Liang, Hanlin Sheng, Xu Si, Hui Gao, Yaxing Li
arxiv-2409-04962.description: Abstract Seismic geobody interpretation is crucial for structural geology studies and various engineering applications. Existing deep learning methods show promise but lack support for multi-modal inputs and struggle to generalize to different geobody types or surveys. We introduce a promptable foundation model for interpreting any geobodies across seismic surveys.

arxiv-2503-08590.title: A counterexample of the Fredholm of Toeplitz operator
arxiv-2503-08590.creator: Liu Hua, Zhang Xinyang
arxiv-2503-08590.description: Abstract . In this paper we study the essential spectra of the Toeplitz operator on the Hardy space H 1 H^{1} . We give a counterexample to show that the Toeplitz operator with symbol is not Fridholm, which give a counterexample to the conjecture by J.A. Virtanen J A in 2006.

arxiv-2505-09832.title: LITMUS : Bayesian Lag Recovery in Reverberation Mapping with Fast Differentiable Models
arxiv-2505-09832.creator: \gn Hugh \sn McDougall 1, \gn Benjamin J. S. \sn Pope 2,1, \gn Tamara M. \sn Davis 1
arxiv-2505-09832.description: Abstract Reverberation mapping is a technique in which the mass of a Seyfert I galaxy’s central supermassive black hole is estimated, along with the system’s physical scale, from the timescale at which variations in brightness propagate through the galactic nucleus.

arxiv-2510-02981.title: Symbol Timing Synchronization and Signal Detection for Ambient Backscatter Communication This work was supported in part by the National Natural Science Foundation of China under Grant 62471388, in part by the Innovation Capability Support Program of Shaanxi under Grant 2024ZC-KJXX-016, and in part
arxiv-2510-02981.creator: Yuxin Li 1 , Guangyue Lu 1 , Yinghui Ye 1 , Zehui Xiong 2 , and Liqin Shi 1
arxiv-2510-02981.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yuxin Li 1 , Guangyue Lu 1 , Yinghui Ye 1 , Zehui Xiong 2 , and Liqin Shi 1. Ambient backscatter communication (AmBC) enables ambient Internet of Things (AIoT) devices to achieve ultra-low-power, low-cost, and massive connectivity. Most existing AmBC studies assume ideal synchronization between the backscatter device (BD) and the backscatter receiver (BR). However, in practice, symbol timing offset (STO) occurs due to both the propagation delay and the BR activation latency, which leads to unreliable symbol recovery at the BR.

britannica-1911-trafalgar-battle-of.title: Trafalgar, Battle of (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-trafalgar-battle-of.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-trafalgar-battle-of.description: Article 'Trafalgar, Battle of' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 27), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. When Villeneuve gave up in despair the attempt to enter the Channel, he steered for Cadiz, and anchored in that port on the 20th of August 1805.

openalex-w7204641318.title: ESCUTA SENSÍVEL NO CUIDADO PSICOLÓGICO PERINATAL DE GESTANTES E PUÉRPERAS INTERNADAS EM LEITOS DE SAÚDE MENTAL
openalex-w7204641318.creator: Valéria Raquel Alcântara Barbosa
openalex-w7204641318.source: OpenAlex / Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação
openalex-w7204641318.description: O artigo buscou analisar a literatura científica sobre escuta sensível como tecnologia relacional no cuidado psicológico perinatal de gestantes e puérperas internadas em leitos de saúde mental. Realizou-se revisão narrativa da literatura, na qual foram incluídos 18 artigos...

pmc-10750057.title: Weaning difficulty after severe pneumonia in adult-onset mitochondrial myopathy with A3243G mutation in the mitochondrial tRNA gene: A case report
pmc-10750057.creator: Xiong Peng, Li-xiu Ma, Ce Xiao, Zhi-zhe Zhang, Min Zhu, Dao-jun Hong, Yi-an Zhan
pmc-10750057.description: BackgroundMitochondrial myopathy is a group of diseases caused by abnormal mitochondrial structure or function. The mitochondrial myopathy impacts muscles of the whole body and exhibits variable symptoms. Respiratory muscle deficits deteriorate pulmonary function in patients with severe pneumonia.Case presentationWe report the case of a male patient with severe pneumonia-induced respiratory failure.

pmc-11340156.title: Ability of parasternal intercostal muscle thickening fraction to predict reintubation in surgical patients with sepsis
pmc-11340156.creator: Mina Adolf Helmy, Ahmed Hasanin, Lydia Magdy Milad, Maha Mostafa, Walid I Hamimy, Rimon S Muhareb, Heba Raafat
pmc-11340156.description: ObjectivesWe aimed to evaluate the ability of the parasternal intercostal (PIC) thickening fraction during spontaneous breathing trial (SBT) to predict the need for reintubation within 48 h after extubation in surgical patients with sepsis.MethodsThis prospective observational study included adult patients with sepsis who were mechanically ventilated and indicated for SBT.

pmc-11413621.title: On the temperature dependent photoluminescence of nanoscale LuPO4:Eu3+ and their application for bioimaging
pmc-11413621.creator: Jan Kappelhoff, Burkhard Greve, Thomas Jüstel
pmc-11413621.description: This work concerns a synthesis method for efficiently luminescent LuPO4:Eu3+ nanoscale particles (∼100 nm) as well as their temperature (77–500 K) and time dependent photoluminescence. In addition, the incubation of these particles into cells of a human lung adenocarcinomic cell line A549 is briefly presented.

pmc-11430037.title: Value of Glycemic Indices for Delayed Cerebral Ischemia after Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage: A Retrospective Single-Center Study
pmc-11430037.creator: Matthias Manfred Deininger, Miriam Weiss, Stephanie Wied, Alexandra Schlycht, Nico Haehn, Gernot Marx, Anke Hoellig, Gerrit Alexander Schubert, Thomas Breuer, Christopher Nimsky
pmc-11430037.description: Delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI) is a severe complication following aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH), linked to poor functional outcomes and prolonged intensive care unit (ICU) stays. Timely DCI diagnosis is crucial but remains challenging. Dysregulated blood glucose, commonly observed after aSAH, may impair the constant glucose supply that is vital for brain function, potentially contributing to DCI.

pmc-11634484.title: Inhibition of CILP2 Improves Glucose Metabolism and Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Sarcopenia via the Wnt Signalling Pathway
pmc-11634484.creator: Zhibo Deng, Chao Song, Long Chen, Rongsheng Zhang, Linhai Yang, Peng Zhang, Yu Xiu, Yibin Su, Fenqi Luo, Jun Luo, Hanhao Dai, Jie Xu
pmc-11634484.description: BackgroundSkeletal muscle is the primary organ involved in insulin‐mediated glucose metabolism. Elevated levels of CILP2 are a significant indicator of impaired glucose tolerance and are predominantly expressed in skeletal muscle. It remains unclear whether CILP2 contributes to age‐related muscle atrophy through regulating the glucose homeostasis and insulin sensitivity.

pmc-11738869.title: Over-Referred and Badly Served – Patient Journeys in Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder at a Community Mental Health Team
pmc-11738869.creator: Samuel Brooks, Delia Annear
pmc-11738869.description: AimsTo measure the proportion of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) referrals that result in a positive diagnosis and medication prescription at a community mental health team (CMHT) in Cardiff.To compare patient journeys from referral to diagnosis – documenting the use of GP mental health liaison, private psychiatrists, questionnaires and CMHT appointments.

pmc-12663670.title: The comparative pathology workbench: An update
pmc-12663670.creator: Michael N. Wicks, Michael Glinka, Bill Hill, Derek Houghton, Bernard Haggarty, Jorge Del-Pozo, Ingrid Ferreira, Florian Jaeckle, David Adams, Shahida Din, Irene Papatheodorou, Kathryn Kirkwood, Albert Burger, Richard A. Baldock, Mark J. Arends
pmc-12663670.description: The Comparative Pathology Workbench (CPW) is a web-browser-based visual analytics platform providing shared access to an interactive “spreadsheet” style presentation of image data and associated analysis data. The software was developed to enable pathologists and other clinical and research users to compare histopathological images of diseased and/or normal tissues between different samples of the same or different patients/species.

pmc-12840217.title: Exploring Temporal Asymmetry in Human Behavior in Social Media Platforms
pmc-12840217.creator: Liang Chen, Heng Zheng, Wenyue Wei, Haoran Pan, Weipeng Nie, Zhifeng Hao, Zhidan Zhao
pmc-12840217.description: With the continuous advancement of information technology, there has been a growing interest in understanding the complexities of human behavior. In particular, asymmetry in human behavior has emerged as a topic of significant theoretical and practical importance. This study focuses on investigating asymmetries in the context of critical time periods, an area that warrants immediate scholarly attention.

pmc-13217070.title: Metrics used in quality improvement publications addressing environmental sustainability in healthcare: a scoping review
pmc-13217070.creator: Colin Sue-Chue-Lam, Sezgi Yanikomeroglu, Darius Baginskis, Doulia M Hamad, Brian M Wong, Nicole Simms, Karen B Born
pmc-13217070.description: ObjectiveQuality improvement (QI) practices and scholarship are increasingly concerned with environmental sustainability given the negative health outcomes caused by the ecological crisis, as well as the environmental impacts of healthcare delivery itself. A core component of QI activities is measuring change. How sustainability metrics have been used in QI is unclear.

pmc-13592050.title: CurT dosage quantitatively affects thylakoid structure and PSII performance in Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803
pmc-13592050.creator: Matthias Ostermeier, Anne‐Christin Pohland, Patrick Reinmöller, Marcel Dann
pmc-13592050.description: SUMMARYThe photosynthetic thylakoid membrane systems of many oxygenic photosynthesizers form elaborate three‐dimensional structures. Curvature Thylakoid (CurT/CURT1) proteins are central regulators of thylakoid architecture in cyanobacteria and plants, driving both grana stacking and the formation of thylakoid convergence zones (TCZs) by promoting membrane curvature while also contributing to green‐algal chloroplast and cyanobacterial cell division.

pmc-13669794.title: Factors Associated With Parent‐Reported Caries in Preschool Children From the KUNO‐Kids Health Study—Repeated Cross‐Sectional Analysis
pmc-13669794.creator: Áine M Lennon, Katharina Fluch‐Maier, K‐A Hiller, Isabelle Schenke, Nils Gade, W Buchalla, Susanne Brandstetter, Angela Köninger, Michael Melter, Christian Apfelbacher, Michael Kabesch, KUNO‐Kids Study group
pmc-13669794.description: ObjectivesThis questionnaire‐based study aimed to assess parent‐reported caries (PRC) at ages 2–5 years and identify potential influencing factors using an exploratory, repeated cross‐sectional analysis within an ongoing birth‐cohort study.MethodsParental factors included health, socioeconomic status, maternal age and dental check‐up attendance.
